app.js uses the shared createModelLoader with immutable revision and disposal hooks. The fail-closed acceptance lifecycle directly retains absent first visit → visible failure/Retry → ready, current cached auto-init, remote-blocked cached inference, recorded-file eviction → partial/Re-download → ready, release/re-init, and verified final cache clear. Mutable stale Update and feature-gated unsupported states are precisely marked not-applicable rather than claimed.

The shared loader presents checking/download/progress/ready/error/Retry/release/clear states in live regions. acceptance-run.json retains the directly exercised lifecycle matrix; corrupt Cache Storage insertion is not separately simulated because response writes are atomic, so missing/evicted recorded responses fail closed as partial.

Each acceptance-run.json route/device cell independently compares initial and changed values for every visible textarea/select/range/checkbox, activates every sample button with a changed target value, requires application change evidence, verifies focus reachability, activates Run with the keyboard, and retains real output. Both Multi-model gate-pass and gate-stop paths are mandatory.
All outputs are posted by worker-protocol responses; multi-model stopped state explicitly says SST-2 was not run and produces no substitute output.

Semantic landmarks/headings, explicit labels, native controls, named buttons, live status, progress, focus-visible design, keyboard activation, and a fail-closed 44px effective-target audit are retained for every mobile cell. Checkbox sizing measures the associated clickable label region. Independent manual screen-reader review remains prudent.

Twenty route/device/theme screenshots plus acceptance-run.json cover automated 1280×800 and 360×740 DPR3 execution with no overflow. Before every capture the validator scrolls all regions, forces content-visibility cards visible, and requires populated result/card/section geometry; screenshots still await independent visual-quality review.

Inference/tokenization/batching/perturbation comparison run in bounded dedicated module workers via WorkerClient; acceptance retains per-run worker latency. A broader real-device INP study remains outside this wave.
